Birds' compact nervous system seems to help them handle tasks very quickly. But avian brains that don’t have a neocortex, so it wasn’t obvious how they made similar decisions. “This was the big question,” said Andreas Nieder, a neurobiologist at the University of Tübingen. “How [would] a differently organized avian brain encode decisions?” To find out, Nieder and his colleague Philipp Schmidbauer put two carrion crows through the same task the monkeys faced, recording their brain activity along the way. The crows solved the task the same way primates do, using the same mathematical logic despite having a very different brain structure. And they did it two times faster.

McAllen, Texas — Benny Melendez, the owner of a small construction company along this stretch of the U.S.-Mexico border, says he's been forced to take drastic measures to protect his immigrant workers. "If I don't install fences, ICE is going to come into my property and take my workers away," Melendez said as he showed CBS News the fencing he's set up at one of the several construction sites he manages in South Texas. Melendez says the fencing is designed to prevent U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents from arresting his workers, and to require them to have judicial warrants before entering his job sites.

Do British pensioners have it better or worse than those in other countries? Getting older is something few of us want to think about. Yet how we fund our later years, and how much we'll get, has been a hot topic. A small-market World Series matchup is not easing tensions between MLB team owners and the players' union on the issue of the salary cap. The Denver Broncos have dominated their all-time series against the Arizona Cardinals. The Broncos and Cardinals have played just 12 times in the regular season in their team histories; the first matchup happened between the then-St. Louis Cardinals and the Broncos in 1973, a game which produced the series' only tie, a 17-17 draw. The difference between the two is how you activate and move your cellular service. Both identify your subscription to a mobile network and feature the same reception and data speed. (AP) — Keelon Russell threw for 311 yards and three touchdowns, including a pair of fourth-quarter scores that helped Alabama pull away, and the 13th-ranked Crimson Tide beat Texas A&M 31-20 on Saturday to end a two-game skid.The Tide (6-2, 4-2 Southeastern Conference) entered the teams’ first meeting since 2023 coming off losses to Georgia and Tennessee. MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — Luke Drzewiecki kicked a 46-yard field goal as time expired, and Minnesota beat No. 15 Iowa 13-10 Saturday to claim the Floyd of Rosedale trophy for the first time since 2023 and second time in 12 years. Drake Lindsey and Jalen Smith connected on a 39-yard pass play on third down from the Minnesota 33 with 39 seconds left to set the Gophers up for the winning points. Held to a season-low 209 yards of offense, Minnesota (5-2, 2-2 Big Ten) also got a third-quarter rushing touchdown from Darius Taylor after an offsides penalty on Iowa negated a fourth-down stop one play earlier.

But the big plays carried North Texas (5-2, 3-0 American) to its fourth straight win.

Established under the Franco dictatorship, the lunchtime ritual is in decline but all is not lost A little before lunchtime each working day across Spain , evidence of one of the lingering, if less notorious, legacies of the Franco dictatorship is carefully traced in chalk, marker pen and printer ink. Beckoning to hungry workers from blackboards, whiteboards and pieces of paper hastily taped to windows, the competitively priced menú del día , or daily set-price lunch, has been part of everyday Spanish life for more than half a century. But while 4m menús are still served each weekday, Spain is slowly losing its appetite for the familiar ritual.

Ebro Ahmed, who acted after driver’s medical emergency, said he hopes incident will show Eritreans ‘in a good way’ A man who hopped on to a school bus full of terrified children that was careering down a Minnesota street after its driver had a medical emergency and manually halted it says he was motivated to act by a Qu’ran verse about how saving one life is equivalent to saving all of humanity. “I’m a numbers guy, and those numbers make sense to me,” Ebro Ahmed, 27, said on Friday during an interview about his actions four days earlier in front of his family’s convenience store in Saint Paul, Minnesota . “I didn’t do it for me. The Renters' Rights Act gives greater flexibility to leave a tenancy but the changes have posed challenges for student landlords. When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords. The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.

At Texas Tech, there is only one voice that matters. And when the de facto team owner isn’t happy, nobody’s happy. Mega-booster Cody Campbell doesn't play, doesn't coach, isn't the athletic director or the school president. But he does have a checkbook that funds Texas Tech's national ambitions through an impressive level of spending on NIL deals. If college football had a Jerry Jones, it would be Campbell. So when Campbell's mad about the state of affairs in Lubbock, everyone should be on high alert. "There is no excuse or reason to lose a game like this," Campbell posted on X after a pretty one-sided 37-24 loss to Cincinnati . "We have to be better."

At boarding school in the early 90s, quietness was seen as weakness. But then I saw the band’s guitarist John Squire making a vast noise while hiding behind a fringe – and learned the strength of understatement I n September 1991, I had just been thrown into the meat-grinder of a Midlands boarding school. In this bear pit, there were predators and there was prey. You were either the swaggering rugby alpha, whipping a wet towel at pale bodies in the eight-boy dormitory; or the homesick ghost, keeping your guard up, endlessly braced for your toilet cubicle to be kicked open or your washbag chucked off the fire escape.

The Warriors’ season is not beginning as hoped. The oldest team in the NBA lost 131-122 to the Phoenix Suns on Saturday, pushing their record to 0-3. It's their first streak of three losses to begin a season since 2007-08, meaning this is the first time they have been 0-3 in Stephen Curry's entire career. Before this season, the Warriors' worst start with Curry was when they went 1-5 to open the 2019-20 season, which is remembered for being the year they were recovering from losing Kevin Durant to free agency and Klay Thompson to an ACL tear before Curry broke his hand in the fourth game. But even in that season, they won their third game.

With expensive World Series ticket prices, some Brewers fans got creative with catching glimpses of the game from stadium windows. In fact, while standing room only tickets had a face value of over $700 for most people, several dozen fans paid $0 to gather just about 10 feet away – at the windows outside the right-field gates of American Family Field during Game 2 on Saturday night, Oct. 24. Nikko Piccione of Cudahy rode his bike and brought an AM/FM radio, a lawn chair and a cigar, and set up camp. "I can buy a lot of cigars with $1,000, and I listen to most of the games anyway," he said. "I just rode my bike out here and I'm going to listen right here, I guess."
